# Actual Cargo manifest lint spelling controls

This isolated outside-product Python variant preserves actual Cargo-generated manifest lint arguments with hyphens, without rewriting their spelling. It adds hyphen to the experimental DATA parser character set in two locations. The exact accepted parent executor, Cargo collector/image and Rust wrapper remain unchanged. This is not a change to RustflagsProjectionV1: the bound native-evidence section3.3 rule admits [a-z0-9_:]+ for projected Rustflags. Native configuration projection must continue to follow that exact bound grammar. The new experiment deals with actual Cargo manifest lint command construction, not projected ambient/config Rustflags and not a new native catalog or public cause.

A new owned firstparty Cargo fixture declares quoted manifest lint names unused-variables, unused-imports, unsafe-code and rust-2018-idioms. Six INFO queries capture the actual joined long arguments. Four fresh controls pass: valid synthetic source completes analysis and metadata; unused-variable source fails under the captured deny; unsafe source fails under the captured forbid; malformed lint DATA refuses before outputs or launch. Three compiler analysis children execute. Original compile_error fixture remains exact and is never compiler input. Full raw graph/command/caller/query/arguments/diagnostics/wait4/metadata and synthetic maps are retained. No accepted control is rerun; no corpus/application/build script/proc macro executes.

Before corpus use this variant requires independent review and exact lead assent.
